FULL AUDIT REPORT - SOFTWARE LICENSE TRUE-UP Q4 2023

Prepared by: IT Asset Management Team
Date: January 18, 2024
Scope: All enterprise software licenses across 3 business units

EXECUTIVE OVERVIEW
We completed a comprehensive audit of all software licenses across the organization. The audit covered 847 distinct software products used by 4,230 employees across Northwind Division, Acme Digital, and Pinnacle Services. The true-up window for our enterprise agreement with our three largest vendors (DataVista, CloudPeak, and StreamLine) closes on February 28, 2024.

SPEND BY PRODUCT CATEGORY
CloudPeak Office Suite: $1.24M annually (1,890 licenses deployed, 2,100 purchased)
DataVista Analytics Platform: $892K annually (412 licenses deployed, 380 purchased)
StreamLine CRM: $654K annually (890 licenses deployed, 950 purchased)
CodeForge Dev Tools: $423K annually (287 licenses deployed, 300 purchased)
SecureVault Endpoint Protection: $312K annually (4,230 licenses deployed, 4,230 purchased - exact match)
Other products (43 total): $1.8M annually

Total annual software spend: $5.32M

OVER-LICENSING DETAILS
CloudPeak Office Suite: 210 unused licenses ($124K annual waste)
- Northwind Division purchased 800 but only using 610
- Acme Digital purchased 700 but only using 640
- Pinnacle Services purchased 600 but only using 640 (under by 40, over by 0 net)
StreamLine CRM: 60 unused licenses ($41K annual waste)
- Primarily in Northwind Division where headcount dropped after the Q2 reorg

Total over-licensing waste: $165K annually

UNDER-LICENSING DETAILS
DataVista Analytics Platform: 32 licenses short ($69K true-up cost)
- Acme Digital has 287 users but only 200 licenses
- Northwind Division has 125 users but only 180 licenses (within limit)
- This has been ongoing since March 2023, risk of audit penalty
SecureVault: compliant (exact match)
CodeForge: 13 licenses short in Pinnacle Services ($18K true-up cost)

Total under-licensing exposure: $87K in true-up costs

RISKS
1. DataVista audit risk: HIGH - we've been under-licensed for 10 months, if DataVista audits us the penalty could be 2-3x the true-up cost ($138K-$207K additional)
2. CloudPeak renewal risk: MEDIUM - their new pricing model (announced Dec 2023) charges per user rather than per license, our renewal in June 2024 could increase costs by 15-20% even with fewer licenses
3. Contract consolidation opportunity: we have 3 separate CloudPeak agreements that could be merged, potential 8% discount but requires 3-year commitment
4. Unknown: we don't know if DataVista has already flagged our account for audit, we requested compliance status from them on Jan 5 but no response yet

DECISION NEEDED
Elena needs to decide:
- True up now ($87K) and reduce CloudPeak licenses (save $165K/year)
- OR renegotiate all three major contracts together before the Feb 28 deadline, which could take 4-6 weeks and might push past the true-up window
- We don't know if renegotiating will get better terms or if we'll lose the true-up option

Write an executive summary for our head of logistics, Ravi, based on this review. He needs to decide on the routing optimization investment.

LAST-MILE DELIVERY COST REVIEW - 2023

Prepared by: Operations Analytics
Date: January 25, 2024
Scope: All last-mile delivery operations across 5 regions

OVERALL METRICS
Total deliveries in 2023: 2.34 million
Total last-mile cost: $31.2M
Average cost per stop: $13.33
Target cost per stop: $11.50
We are 15.9% over target

COST PER STOP BY REGION
Northeast: $15.87 per stop (412K deliveries) - 38% over target
- High congestion, parking violations averaging $2.10 per stop
- Driver wait times average 8.3 minutes per stop (vs 4.1 min company average)
- Union labor rates 22% above national average

Southeast: $11.24 per stop (518K deliveries) - 2.3% under target
- Best performing region
- Lower labor costs, suburban density works well with current routing

Midwest: $12.45 per stop (487K deliveries) - 8.3% over target
- Long distances between stops (average 4.2 miles vs 2.1 miles company average)
- Rural routes not well optimized, 31% of stops require >6 mile detours

Southwest: $13.92 per stop (523K deliveries) - 21% over target
- Extreme heat causes vehicle AC costs (+$0.85 per stop)
- High driver turnover (47% annual), training costs $1.40 per stop
- New housing developments not in routing database

West Coast: $14.56 per stop (400K deliveries) - 26.6% over target
- Highest labor costs in the network
- Regulatory compliance (emissions, labor rules) adds $1.20 per stop
- Port congestion causes delays on 18% of routes

ROOT CAUSES
1. Routing algorithm hasn't been updated since 2021, doesn't account for real-time traffic or new construction
2. Driver app doesn't support dynamic rerouting, drivers follow static sequences
3. Northeast and West Coast labor costs are structural, can't be reduced without operational changes
4. We don't know the exact cost of parking violations - our records show $2.10 per Northeast stop but drivers report they sometimes pay out of pocket and don't expense it

OPTIONS
A. Invest in new routing optimization platform - $2.4M implementation + $480K/year, estimated 12-18% cost reduction across all regions, 8-month implementation
B. Switch Northeast and West Coast to gig-driver model for 40% of stops - saves $3.20 per stop on those routes but increases quality risk, $800K to set up
C. Add locker/drop-point network in high-cost urban areas - $1.8M capital investment, reduces per-stop cost by $4.50 for locker deliveries, but only 22% of stops are locker-eligible
D. Do nothing - maintain current operations, accept $13.33 average cost per stop

DECISION NEEDED
Ravi needs to decide which option(s) to pursue. The board has allocated $3M for operational improvements in 2024 but we don't know if they'll approve ongoing costs beyond that. Option A has the broadest impact but takes longest to implement.

Write an executive summary for Ravi.
